1.why: All six screens show a static layout with no animations, moving images, or pop-up dialogs.

2.why: Large bold headings and high-contrast blue primary buttons make the main actions and titles stand out clearly.

3.why: Each step is a single focused form with a clear title and progress tabs, though the persistent Logs panel adds minor clutter.

4.why: The user must carry forward multiple values (email/phone, recovery token, MFA code) across separate screens and also recall password complexity rules.

5.why: No password-manager affordances, autofill indicators, or “remember me” options appear on any screen.

6.why: No saved-account lists, pre-filled familiar values, or other recognition aids for previously used items are shown.

7.why: Most instructional text is concise and readable, although the Stay-safe and privacy paragraphs are somewhat long.

8.why: No error messages appear in any of the provided screenshots, so they cannot be said to describe problems or fixes.

9.why: Password rules are listed as requirements but no example values are given, and other input fields lack example placeholders.

10.why: The flow offers only a single password-recovery path and never presents choices such as password, code, or face login.

11.why: Each screen presents essentially one primary action and at most one secondary control, avoiding choice overload.

12.why: The final screen clearly states success, yet intermediate steps show no explicit confirmation of the outcome of each action.

13.why: A persistent Stay-safe tip box and brief step-specific instructions appear on every screen.

14.why: Fields can be re-entered and the last screen has a return button, but no explicit back or retry controls are visible on intermediate steps.

15.why: All six steps share the identical header, progress tabs, card layout, Stay-safe panel, and Logs styling.
